# Complete a private secondary share sale

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When an existing holder proposes to sell privately held company shares to another investor. An authorized completed transfer or documented no-go, with reconciled consideration and ownership records.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Identify the shares, parties and proposed terms

agent-runnable


Gather ownership evidence, instrument type, acquisition history, seller and buyer identities, price and proposed timetable. Distinguish a sale of existing shares from new company fundraising or an unexercised option.

- Sources: [SEC private secondary markets](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/capital-raising-building-blocks/private-secondary-markets)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Determine transfer restrictions and the legal route

human · human approval required


Counsel reviews governing documents, rights of first refusal, approvals, securities restrictions and the affected jurisdictions. Record required waivers, diligence and tax advice; do not treat private shares as freely tradable.

- Sources: [SEC private secondary markets](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/capital-raising-building-blocks/private-secondary-markets)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the diligence and transfer pack

agent-runnable


Reconcile the seller's holding and assemble approved disclosures, transfer documents and a conditions checklist. Keep sensitive company information restricted and separate seller proceeds from money payable to the company.

- Sources: [SEC private secondary markets](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/capital-raising-building-blocks/private-secondary-markets)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve and execute closing

human · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized parties satisfy the documented approvals and conditions, sign the approved documents and verify settlement instructions independently. Follow the agreed closing sequence and retain evidence before treating funds or shares as transferred.

- Sources: [SEC private secondary markets](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/capital-raising-building-blocks/private-secondary-markets)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile the register and reporting follow-up

agent-runnable


Match the completed transfer, payment evidence and updated ownership records. Issue approved confirmations, track unresolved conditions and route tax or securities reporting to the responsible professionals.

- Verify: An authorized completed transfer or documented no-go, with reconciled consideration and ownership records.
- Sources: [SEC private secondary markets](https://www.sec.gov/resources-small-businesses/capital-raising-building-blocks/private-secondary-markets)
